subject: Making `%+%` more indulgent (i.e. not breaking previous definitions of the same operator)

messages.author: 639970b1c93a337f
messages.subject: Making `%+%` more indulgent (i.e. not breaking previous definitions of the same operator)
parts:
Right now `%+%` is defined in such a way that it calls `+.gg` if the first argument is `theme` or `ggplot`, otherwise just returns NULL. If `%+%` was previously defined in another package, loading `ggplot2` package will break it - but I don't see why this is necessary if they work with non-overlapping classes. I tried changing the following in the `plot-construction.r` source file: instead of definition `"%+%" <- `+.gg`` (line 54), I put the following:
"%+%" <- function(...) UseMethod("%+%")
"%+%.theme" <- `+.gg`
"%+%.ggplot" <- `+.gg`
(of course don't forget adding corresponding `export()` instructions to the `NAMESPACE`)

I have built and loaded this fork and it works as expected: now I can load another package (where `%+%` is defined to work with `character` class), then load `ggplot2`, and they both work correctly. Is there any special reason of not implementing this?

P.S. I have asked this question (in more extended way) at StackOverflow - you can also comment or answer there.
